title: Best Dehumidifier for Hurricane Season (2026): Outages & Cleanup
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for Hurricane Season, Power Outages and Storm Cleanup
dek: Storm season tests a dehumidifier three ways: muggy weeks before, power cuts during and wet floors after. These picks are built for all three.
description: The best dehumidifiers for hurricane season: auto-restart units for power outages, generator-friendly picks and an AlorAir Storm LGR for drying out after.
intro: The **best dehumidifier for hurricane season** isn't simply the biggest one. It's the one that keeps your home dry through weeks of tropical humidity, comes back on by itself when the power flickers, runs on a generator without tripping it, and doesn't leave a full bucket sitting in a house you've evacuated. For most households, our top pick is the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1**: a true 50-pint unit that restarts at your settings after an outage, drains through a hose and lets you check humidity from your phone.

This guide is for homeowners in hurricane-prone areas, from the Gulf Coast to the Carolinas, who want to buy once and be ready. The three things that matter most are auto-restart and a drainage setup that works unattended; a running draw your generator or battery can actually handle; and, if water does get in, access to a low-grain refrigerant (LGR) unit like the **AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme** to dry the structure fast.
topPicksLead: The **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** is our top hurricane-season pick: 50 pints a day, automatic restart after power cuts and Wi-Fi monitoring.

products.whyWeLoveIt: Hurricane season is as much about the soggy weeks around a storm as the storm itself. This Frigidaire has the capacity for a whole lower level, and when a squall line knocks out power for an hour, it comes back on with your humidity setting instead of sitting idle.

With a gravity hose to a floor drain it runs for days unattended. More models are in our [best Frigidaire dehumidifier](/best/best-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) guide.

Compare other self-draining models in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

products.whyWeLoveIt: During a multi-day outage, every watt counts. A 22-pint compressor unit draws far less than a basement model, so it can keep one room, such as a bedroom or the room where you've stacked important papers, out of mold territory on a modest generator.

Room units this size typically run at roughly 230–260 watts with the compressor on, versus 400–560 watts for a 50-pint model, per our [dehumidifier electricity guide](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/). It restarts at your settings when power returns and drains through a hose to a nearby tub or sink.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for hurricane season

blocks.text: We don't lab-test, and we don't simulate storms. We compare DOE 2019 and AHAM ratings, published running watts and amps, manuals for auto-restart behavior, ENERGY STAR listings and CPSC recalls, then read owner reviews for how units behave after outages: do they come back on, do pumps resume, and do apps reconnect? Every pick is a verified Amazon listing.

sections.heading: How to choose a dehumidifier for storm season

items.label: Auto-restart that remembers settings
items.text: This is the single most important feature. Without it, a two-second flicker can switch your dehumidifier off until you notice. After you buy, test it: unplug the unit while it runs, plug it back in and see what it does.

items.label: Drainage that doesn't need you
items.text: If you might evacuate, the unit must drain continuously.
sub: Floor drain or sump below the unit: gravity hose
Bucket only: fine for daily use, not for being away

items.label: Running watts you can back up
items.text: Check the listed watts or amps (amps × 120 ≈ watts). A 20–22 pint unit is far easier on a generator than a 50-pint basement model.

items.label: Remote monitoring, with realistic expectations
items.text: Wi-Fi models let you watch humidity from an evacuation hotel, but only while power and internet are up at home.

items.label: A plan for real water
items.text: Household units maintain humidity; they don't dry soaked walls. Know whether you'll buy an LGR unit, [rent one](/guides/dehumidifier-rental/) or call a restoration company.

sections.heading: Running a dehumidifier on a generator or battery

blocks.text: A dehumidifier's compressor draws a steady load while running, plus a short surge each time it starts. Add up the running watts of everything you plan to power, leave headroom for those startup surges, and check both the running and surge ratings on your generator.

blocks.text: Battery power stations are better for short gaps than multi-day outages: even a 22-pint unit can drain a 1,000 Wh station in a few hours of compressor time. If you're planning solar or a long-term battery setup, our [off-grid dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-off-grid/) guide goes deeper.

blocks.title: Generator safety
blocks.text: Run generators outdoors only, never in a garage, basement or porch, even with doors open, and keep them at least 20 feet from windows, doors and vents. Use working carbon monoxide alarms inside. Use heavy-duty outdoor extension cords, and never plug a generator into a wall outlet.

sections.heading: After the storm: drying out a wet house

items: **Stay safe first.** Don't plug anything into outlets or power strips that were underwater, and have an electrician check flooded circuits before use.
**Document the damage.** Photograph wet areas and damaged items before you move or remove them, for your insurer.
**Remove what can't be saved.** Soaked carpet pad, insulation and the bottom of wet drywall usually have to go; cutting them out lets the framing dry.
**Close the space and dry it.** Run an LGR dehumidifier with fans aimed at wet surfaces, doors and windows shut, and drain to a sink or outside.
**Measure, don't guess.** A moisture meter tells you when wood and drywall are back to normal readings; compare with an unaffected room.

**Watch for mold.** Musty odors or spots after a few days mean the drying isn't keeping up. Our guide to [whether a dehumidifier helps with mold](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-help-with-mold/) explains when to call a pro.
Clean or replace the filter and check hoses and pump lines for kinks before the season starts.
Test auto-restart by unplugging the running unit and plugging it back in.
In a flood-prone basement, plan to unplug the unit and carry it upstairs if water is forecast.
Keep a spare drain hose and a hygrometer on hand.
Set a target around 50% and let the humidistat work through the muggy weeks; our [humid climates guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-humid-climates/) covers everyday setups.
**You want one reliable unit for the lower level, with a floor drain:** the Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1.
**Your home is on a slab or the drain is uphill:** the Waykar YDZ-150PM with its built-in pump.
**You often evacuate and want to keep an eye on the house:** the hOmeLabs HME031003N.
**You'll rely on a small generator for days:** the Frigidaire FFAD2233W1 for the one room that matters most.
**You live where flooding is a real risk:** keep an AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme on hand, or know where to rent an LGR.

blocks.text: Prepare for hurricane season with a dehumidifier that restarts on its own, drains without you and runs within your backup power. The Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1 does all three for most homes, the Waykar adds a pump, and the 22-pint Frigidaire stretches a small generator further. If water gets inside, an LGR such as the AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme, running within the first day or two, is what keeps a wet house from becoming a moldy one.

faqs.q: Can I run a dehumidifier on a generator?
faqs.a: Yes. Add up the running watts of everything you'll power and leave headroom for the compressor's startup surge. A 22-pint unit (about 230–260 W) is easy on a small inverter generator; a 50-pint unit (about 400–560 W) needs a mid-size one. Always run the generator outdoors, well away from the house.

faqs.q: Will my dehumidifier turn back on after a power outage?
faqs.a: Only if it has auto-restart. Most current models from Frigidaire, hOmeLabs and Waykar resume at their last settings, but test yours by unplugging it while it runs. Some pump units may need pump mode re-selected afterward.

faqs.q: Do I need a dehumidifier after a hurricane?
faqs.a: If any water got inside, yes, and fast: wet materials should be dried within 24–48 hours to limit mold. For soaked drywall, floors or carpet, use an LGR dehumidifier with fans, or call a restoration company for large areas.

faqs.q: What is the AlorAir Storm dehumidifier best for?
faqs.a: AlorAir's Storm line is built for restoration work: drying flooded basements, crawl spaces and job sites. The Storm LGR Extreme is rated at 85 pints a day (AHAM) with a built-in pump. It's more machine than you need for everyday humidity control.

faqs.q: How many watts does a dehumidifier use during an outage?
faqs.a: The same as any other time: roughly 230–260 W for a 20–22 pint room unit and 400–560 W for a 50-pint model while the compressor runs, plus a brief surge at startup. LGR units like the Storm LGR Extreme draw more, about 5.4 amps.

faqs.q: Do I need a dehumidifier for a storm shelter?
faqs.a: Underground shelters and safe rooms often get damp between storms. If there's power, a small compressor unit keeps them dry; if not, renewable desiccant packs plus regular airing out work well for a small space.
